We chucked them in the bin together then and she drank from a beaker for all her drinks from then on, she was just coming up for 2 at the time.  I hope you manage to get your LO onto a beaker for his milk soon hun.  The cow beaker is a great idea!  Xx

Some kids just take awhile longer to outgrow certain comforts. As long as he's not going to sleep with bottle in his mouth and he's using a sippy or other cups at other times, then I don't see a problem.
Everyone is right about brushing his teeth. But just becareful not to do that too often. Too much brushing can cause receding gum lines and tooth enamel erosion. Plus too much toothpaste is not good either.
twice a day is good enough for most people.

Kailey has been off bottles for a few months. i had the avent bottles, but she always chewed holes in the teats. one day i got sick of it and went out and bought some plastic cups and a new sipper cup. it didnt bother her at all, but she had already been used to drinking out of a cup since she was alot younger.
i dont think there is anything wrong with him still having a bottle. he will grow out of it. my advice would be give him the bottle before he goes to his bed, or before he gets too tired. it may be a comfort thing, and if he doesnt have it when he is unhappy or tired, he may realise he doesnt need the comfort any longer.
Good Luck, but i wouldnt be too worried!!

Yeah I agree with some of the other replies about risking tooth decay. Bottles are not like breastfeeding so he really shouldn't have a bottle at this age but he might really need the comfort. Im still breastfeeding at 2 but there is not as much of a risk of tooth decay and I really feel that children of this age still need the comfort and reassurence but maybe it shouldn't be from a bottle. Could you try giving him loadsa cuddles with his bottles and slowly cut down on them but keep the cuddles?
I wouldn't do it before he goes to bed as this is the highest risk time for tooth decay.

Thanks girls
